issue: Cloze '___ lavorare domani mattina?' has no subject or context; distractor 'puoi' (same 'tu' person, different modal) forms an equally grammatical, meaningful Italian sentence ('Puoi lavorare domani mattina?'), so the keyed answer 'devi' is not uniquely correct.
fix: Add disambiguating context (e.g. an English translation cue 'You must work tomorrow morning?' or a preceding sentence establishing obligation) so only one modal verb is correct.

issue: Cloze '___ tornare a casa presto.' has no subject/context; distractor 'dobbiamo' (same 'noi' person, different modal) is an equally valid, grammatical Italian sentence, so 'vogliamo' is not uniquely correct.
fix: Add a translation cue or context sentence that specifies obligation vs. desire so only one modal is correct.

issue: 'I ragazzi ___ partire domani.' distractor 'possono' (same 'loro' person, different modal) produces an equally grammatical sentence ('I ragazzi possono partire domani'), so 'devono' is not uniquely correct without context.
fix: Add context/translation specifying obligation (must) vs. ability (can) so the keyed modal is uniquely determined.

issue: '___ dormire un po' di più?' gives no subject; besides the modal ambiguity (vuoi/dovete both grammatical), the item also mixes a person mismatch (vuoi=tu vs. correct volete=voi) with nothing in the sentence indicating whether one or multiple people are addressed.
fix: Specify the subject/person via context (e.g. include 'Ragazzi, ...') or an English cue, and keep distractors to genuine grammar errors rather than an alternate valid person/modal.

issue: 'Anna ___ finire il progetto.' distractor 'può' (same 'lei' person, different modal) forms an equally grammatical sentence ('Anna può finire il progetto'), so 'deve' is not uniquely correct without further context.
fix: Add context/translation clarifying obligation vs. ability so only the keyed modal fits.

issue: '___ studiare stasera.' has no subject; 'posso' (same implied 'io' person, different modal) and 'deve' (different person, but still a grammatically complete sentence) both produce valid Italian, leaving 'devo' not uniquely determined.

issue: '___ uscire stasera con noi?' distractor 'vuoi' (same 'tu' person, different modal) is an equally grammatical, natural question ('Vuoi uscire stasera con noi?'), so 'puoi' is not uniquely correct.

issue: 'Marco ___ mangiare una pizza.' distractor 'deve' (same 'lui' person, different modal) is an equally grammatical sentence ('Marco deve mangiare una pizza'), so 'vuole' is not uniquely correct without context.

issue: '___ entrare, per favore?' distractor 'vogliamo' (same 'noi' person, different modal) is grammatically valid ('Vogliamo entrare, per favore?'), so 'possiamo' is not uniquely correct without context.

issue: Error-correction item marks 'Oggi è ventidue di marzo.' as wrong, keeping only 'Oggi è il ventidue marzo.' as correct. In practice 'il ventidue di marzo' (with 'di') is also commonly used and accepted in natural spoken/written Italian, so labeling it a grammar error is arguably too strict/prescriptive.
fix: Either accept both 'il ventidue marzo' and 'il ventidue di marzo' as correct, or reframe the item to test the missing definite article (the clearer, unambiguous error) rather than the presence of 'di'.
